referents.why: 'me' in 'honor yourself over me' is Moses, the speaker of his own words to Pharaoh; a first person inside a speech is its speaker.
'you' in 'I will pray for you' is second masculine singular inside Moses's speech; the addressee is Pharaoh.
'your officials': second masculine singular possessor in Moses's speech, the addressee Pharaoh.
'your people': possessor is the addressee Pharaoh.
'from you': second masculine singular in Moses's speech, addressee Pharaoh.
'your houses': possessor is the addressee Pharaoh.
the implied 'you' of the command 'honor yourself' is the person the command is spoken to, Pharaoh.
'I will pray' is first person common singular in Moses's speech.
third feminine plural 'they will remain only in the Nile' agrees with the frogs (feminine plural) that are being removed.

links.why: The lamed infinitive 'to cut off the frogs' gives what the prayer asks for. After a verb of speaking (pray) the infinitive is what is said, which the purpose rule excludes; it is recorded as content instead.
links.category: infinitive after a verb of speech

links.why: Pray is a clause of saying; the infinitive gives what is asked (R1). Also keeps the petition content inside the turn.
links.category: infinitive after a verb of speech

links.why: cl5 is not a clause of this verse, and a then link is within a verse only (across verses is the episode rung).
Moses said; the imperative 'honor yourself over me' is the first said clause of his speech (R1).

groups.why: Moses speaks to Pharaoh; the speech holds cl1, cl2 and the parenthetical cl4. Sender and addressee are correct (R2).

none_fit.where: cl4, 'only in the River they will remain', inside Moses's question
none_fit.what: a restriction on what the removal covers (the frogs removed except those that stay in the Nile). No link type carries an exception to a purpose clause: 'unless' is a condition, and 'but_rather' needs a negative clause with כִּי אִם.
